ling-phon-01-c1.text: Ian Maddieson (2013). Consonant-Vowel Ratio. The World Atlas of Language Structures Online (Max Planck Institute for Evolutionary Anthropology), chapter 3.
ling-phon-01-c1.quote: The ratio thus ranges between 1.11 and 29
ling-phon-01-c1.claim: Most languages have more consonants than vowels, but the ratio varies a great deal.

ling-phon-05-c2.quote: first described in 1818 by the Danish philologist Rasmus Rask (1787–1832) and set out in detail in 1822 by the German philologist Jacob Grimm (1785–1863)
ling-phon-05-c2.claim: In the early 1800s, Jacob Grimm (yes, of fairy-tale fame), building on Rasmus Rask's 1818 observations, formulated a systematic shift between Proto-Indo-European (PIE) and the Germanic languages.
